Edit the collision of the loaded asset or object: reshape it, see and paint the material of each face, or build it from the model's own meshes.
The Collision tool needs the Vulkan renderer.

Reshape the model's collision with the vertex brush.

1. Choose the Layer above the tabs, then Start Collision Edit.
2. Pick a Brush mode (Raise, Lower, Drag or Smooth) and its Radius. Move the mouse over the collision: the sphere shows what the brush reaches.
3. Hold the left mouse button to brush. Raise, Lower and Smooth apply again at each interval while it is held; Drag slides the vertices under the brush with the mouse at their height.
4. Commit (above the tabs) rebuilds the collision as one action that can be undone; Discard puts the vertices back. Save the model to write it.

1. Choose the Layer above the tabs. While this tab is open, each face is drawn in the colour of its material; the Legend lists them, with how many faces have each.
2. Select mode shows the material of the face clicked, and its hit material ID can be typed in freely. To paint, choose the material by Surface and Property, from the Legend, or with Pick.
3. Start Material Paint, then hold the left mouse button over the collision. A Radius of 0 paints the face under the cursor; a larger one paints the faces within it, limited by the Facing Limit.
4. Commit (above the tabs) rebuilds the collision with its new materials as one action that can be undone; Discard puts them back. Save the model to write it.
Build the model's collision from its own meshes.

1. Tick the meshes to build from. A mesh whose material is named hkm_Name_Property gets that collision material; the others get the Collision Material chosen.
2. Simplify reduces the detail of the mesh, if it is on.
3. Tick the layers to build. A layer with a file has its mesh replaced; an asset's layer without one gets a new file, based on the other layer's.
4. Build Collision makes it as one action that can be undone. Save the model to write it; a new file is added to its binder then (the binder is made if the layer had none).
